CIGO EXECUTION TASK — CIGO-P2-BLOCK1

MAJOR PART
Part 2 — Data Access, Integration & Evidence Layer

BLOCK
Operational Read Contracts + Evidence Ingestion Boundary

OBJECTIVE
Build CIGO's first provider-neutral data-access and evidence-ingestion kernel. CIGO must be able to consume authorized operational observations as structured evidence without taking ownership of Business OS/MVP operational data, without direct provider calls, and without weakening workspace isolation.

AUTHORITATIVE BOUNDARIES
- Writable repository: sohail654312-gif/codeedge-intelligent-growth-os only.
- Business OS remains the operational system of record.
- MVP and Business OS are read-only references.
- CIGO may ingest authorized projections/evidence, but must not write into protected operational stores.
- No direct Twilio/Meta/Vapi/OpenAI/Stripe/ERPNext/provider implementation in this block.
- No live external integration is required yet; establish contracts and a deterministic in-memory/demo adapter first.
- Reuse the completed Part 1 truth kernel. Do not redefine or bypass its ownership, workspace, provenance, authority or truth-class rules.

SELECTED REFERENCES
1. codeedge-business-os — inspect only materially relevant patterns for workspace scope, operational ownership, provider-neutral interfaces/adapters, Demo/Sandbox/Production execution modes, external-effect policy and read-model/API boundaries.
2. codeedge — inspect only tenant-isolation/RLS/testing patterns useful for defensive workspace enforcement.
Do not inspect unrelated reference repositories unless a concrete dependency emerges.

REQUIRED ARTIFACTS
A. Architecture documentation:
- docs/architecture/DATA-ACCESS-EVIDENCE-BOUNDARY.md
- docs/architecture/INTEGRATION-CONTRACTS.md

The docs must define:
- authorized read boundary;
- source-system identity and source record references;
- workspace/tenant authority;
- read request/read result semantics;
- freshness/staleness;
- cursor/checkpoint semantics;
- partial-result and error semantics;
- evidence normalization;
- duplicate/idempotency approach;
- source-of-truth preservation;
- demo/sandbox parity;
- read-only operational boundary;
- future live-adapter insertion point.

B. Executable TypeScript integration/evidence kernel, framework-independent and provider-neutral. A clean structure such as:
- src/integration/contracts.ts
- src/integration/source-reader.ts
- src/integration/in-memory-source-reader.ts
- src/evidence/normalize.ts
- src/evidence/fingerprint.ts
- src/evidence/validation.ts
- src/integration/index.ts
Naming may be adjusted if a cleaner structure is justified.

The kernel must model at minimum:
- AuthorizedWorkspaceContext.
- OperationalSource / source-system identity compatible with Part 1 SourceSystem.
- SourceRecordReference with external ID/version or stable external reference.
- ReadRequest including workspace, resource kind, optional cursor and bounded limit.
- ReadResult with records, next cursor, observed/fetched timestamp, completeness/partial state and explicit errors.
- SourceReader interface that is read-only.
- InMemorySourceReader/demo adapter for deterministic tests.
- Evidence normalization into Part 1 Evidence records.
- Stable fingerprint/idempotency helper so the same source observation can be recognized deterministically.
- Freshness/staleness metadata or helper.
- Explicit validation results/errors rather than silent coercion.

MANDATORY INVARIANTS / ACCEPTANCE TESTS
1. Every read request requires an authorized workspace context.
2. A SourceReader result containing records from another workspace is rejected.
3. Operational source records remain EXTERNAL_OPERATIONAL; normalization must never convert them into CIGO-owned operational truth.
4. Normalized evidence must preserve source system, external reference, workspace and timestamps.
5. Missing source reference/provenance must fail validation.
6. Re-reading the exact same source observation produces the same stable fingerprint/idempotency key.
7. A changed source version/value produces a different fingerprint or explicit new observation identity.
8. Partial/incomplete reads and errors are explicit in ReadResult and cannot be mistaken for complete data.
9. Demo/in-memory adapter uses the same contracts and tenancy rules expected of future production adapters.
10. The integration/evidence kernel contains no direct provider SDK/API implementation.
11. Existing Part 1 tests continue to pass.
12. Typecheck/build and new deterministic tests pass.

TESTS
Add deterministic tests, preferably in a new file such as:
- test/integration-evidence.test.mjs
and keep existing truth tests intact.

REFERENCE REPORT
In one architecture document include a “Reference patterns used” section describing:
- which Business OS/MVP patterns were used conceptually;
- what was deliberately not copied;
- why the block stops at contracts + deterministic adapter rather than a live operational integration.

VERIFICATION / EVIDENCE
Run the repository verification needed to prove:
- existing Part 1 truth tests still pass;
- new integration/evidence tests pass;
- TypeScript typecheck/build pass.
Record exact changed files, commands/results and resulting commit SHAs in a new evidence file:
- ops/evidence/CIGO-P2-BLOCK1.md

COMPLETION RULE
Mark COMPLETE_FOR_PLANNER only when docs, executable contracts/kernel, deterministic adapter, tests and evidence exist in the CIGO repo and all required verification passes. A document-only or interface-only result is INCOMPLETE.

DO NOT
- modify protected/reference repositories;
- build live provider integrations;
- build CRM/booking/finance/communications duplicates;
- add operational writes;
- weaken Part 1 tenant/ownership/provenance rules;
- treat external-source data as CIGO-owned operational truth.
